AR coefficients for forecast updating

Source: R/response_time.R
ar_from_response_time.Rd

Two sources of third-order AR coefficients for error post-processing, in the Deltares sign convention used by error_updater() and by the Environment Agency's IMFS: the error at step t is a1 times the error at t - 1, plus a2 times that at t - 2, plus a3 times that at t - 3.

Usage

ar_from_response_time(decay_h, dt, first_coefficient = 1.765)

ar_ea_default()

Arguments

decay_h

Principal decay time in hours, typically pdm_response_time()$time_to_peak_h.

dt

Model time step in hours.

first_coefficient

The fixed first coefficient of the family.

Value

A named numeric vector a_1, a_2, a_3 with attribute roots.

Details

ar_ea_default() gives the Environment Agency 2024 default set, defined for 15-minute steps.

ar_from_response_time() builds a member of the continuous default family from one timescale, the principal decay time. It follows the published construction of reach.postproc::default_family_ar_parameters(): the first coefficient is fixed at 1.765; a rapid negative root decays in a third of a step; the principal root is exp(-1 / decay) with the decay in steps; the remaining root makes the three sum to the first coefficient. As in reach.postproc, equating a catchment's time to peak with the decay of its forecast errors is an approximation, a starting estimate to be checked against past events, not a derived result. Check any set with reach.postproc::assess() before operational use.

See also

pdm_response_time(), pdm_hindcast()

Examples

ar_ea_default()
#>       a_1       a_2       a_3 
#>  1.765000 -0.726250 -0.040656 
ar_from_response_time(9, dt = 0.25)
#>         a_1         a_2         a_3 
#>  1.76500000 -0.72875763 -0.04078111 
#> attr(,"roots")
#> [1]  0.97260448  0.84218259 -0.04978707
